name: Mathematics
description: 12 credits of math beyond what is already used elsewhere in the CSCE degree plan.
notes: Credits must be in addition to degree-plan math; Math minor alone doesn’t satisfy the full 12 emphasis hours, but this emphasis can also fulfill the Math minor credits with grades of C or better.

name: Business
description: Follow Business minor courses; emphasis can be completed without finishing the minor.
notes: Only two additional classes beyond degree-plan overlap are typically needed to finish the Business minor.

name: Art
description: Complete the Minor in Art (Department of Visualization).

rules.track_guidance: Use traditional media emphasis if aiming for the Visualization MS program.

notes: All courses should come from the official Art minor plan.

name: Foreign Languages
description: 12 hours of foreign language courses (100–200 level allowed).
notes: These hours are separate from the core foreign language requirement already satisfied elsewhere.

name: Cybersecurity
description: 12 hours from the approved non-CSCE Cybersecurity minor list (interdisciplinary track recommended).

rules.course_list_source: Non-CSCE courses approved for the Cybersecurity minor

notes: Emphasis typically requires at least one more class than the Cybersecurity minor; declaring the minor can improve access to courses.

name: Game Design and Development
description: 12 hours from the approved non-CSCE Game minor course list.

rules.course_list_source: Non-CSCE courses approved for the Game minor

notes: Declaring the Game minor may ease access to VIST classes.

name: Neuroscience
description: 12 hours from the approved Neuroscience minor non-CSCE course list.

rules.course_list_source: Non-CSCE courses approved for the Neuroscience minor

notes: Declaring the Neuroscience minor may ease access to courses.

name: STEM Areas
description: Sequence of upper-level courses from a STEM department (service courses excluded).
notes: Courses cannot double count toward other degree requirements.

name: Liberal Arts & Social Sciences
description: Upper-level courses in liberal arts/social sciences (e.g., digital humanities, technical writing, music, history, philosophy, foreign languages, social sciences).
notes: Mark qualifying liberal arts or social sciences courses as 'Count toward emphasis' in your Academic Record. Include upper-division courses where possible.

name: Other / Double Degree / Post-baccalaureate
description: Use credits from another degree/major when applicable.
notes: Apply credits from the other program if available and adviser-approved.
